title: Performance signature publishing operator and data retention playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As we scale Redwood-verified performance profiles across an expanding model catalog, we need an operator-level publishing workflow and a clear retention/stewardship playbook for the performance signatures (latency, throughput, cost, and footprint metadata). Current publish flows are manual PR-driven artifacts and ad-hoc telemetry attachments which cause stale profiles, inconsistent metadata, and long verification cycles for small model updates.

Goal: Create an operator that automates profile publish + attestation steps, captures the minimum telemetry contract required for future regression detection, and codifies retention/archival rules so we can lean on automation for profile lifecycle management. This ticket coordinates the PM spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and initial runbook for SRE/Platform stewards.

Scope:
- Define required performance signature fields (p90 latency on typical seqs, throughput per GPU type, normalized token-cost metric, batch sensitivity, kv-cache warmup cost).
- Publish operator that: validates signature completeness, attaches sample test vectors and traces, signs the profile (internal provenance header), and creates a git-backed artifact in the verified-profile registry.
- Retention and archival rules: active profiles (<=12 months since last verification) vs. archived (>12 months), auto-sampling schedule, and re-verification triggers (model version change, kernel change, runtime flag change).
- Telemetry contract: minimal set of metrics (latency p50/p90/p99, throughput, failure_rate, cost_per_1000_tokens, sample_prompt_hash) emitted by benchmark harness and persisted to profile metadata.
- Rollback/abort paths: automated rollback on publish if post-publish smoke fails in staging; manual steward override explained in runbook.

Acceptance criteria: [list]
- Operator validates and accepts a performance signature that includes all required fields and sample vectors.
- Profiles written to the verified registry include cryptographic provenance (signer, commit hash, timestamp) and a link to the benchmark run and PR.
- Telemetry contract is defined and implemented in the benchmark harness (eng PR merged).
- Retention policy is encoded as a scheduled job (cron) that marks profiles as archived and emits an alert if >20% of active profiles are older than expected.
- Runbook exists and is reviewed by SRE, Security, and Legal (compliance appendix).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We prefer a git-backed artifact approach (lightweight, auditable) instead of inserting heavy records into internal DBs to keep rollback simple. Tradeoff: searching and aggregating cross-repo metadata will require an indexer, plan included below.
- Cryptographic provenance will use our existing signing key rotation scheme; initial MVP uses internal signing only (customer-facing signatures TBD for enterprise later).
- Retention window set at 12 months to balance storage/operational cost vs. drift detection sensitivity. A follow-up ticket will evaluate a decay-based strategy keyed by model usage.

Implementation plan:
1) PM: finalize telemetry contract and required signature fields; publish spec doc (link below).
2) ENG (Benchmarking team): extend harness to emit the contract and attach sample traces (ENG-23114).
3) ENG (Platform): implement operator to ingest signature payload, validate, sign, and create git artifact + indexer event (ENG-23899).
4) DevOps: schedule retention cron and implement archival mark + notification (ENG-24202).
5) Docs/Console: expose profile status (active/archived) and provenance UI in Console (PM-Runtime Console changes).

Runbook highlights:
- Pre-publish checks: unit test verification, sample trace presence, signer key check.
- Post-publish smoke: automated validation against canary runtime (5-minute run, sample prompts). If failure -> operator triggers rollback and files incident in PagerDuty.
- Steward actions: how to re-run verification, how to force-unarchive, how to tag profiles with deprecation reasons.

Telemetry contract (summary): [list]
- profile_id: unique id (uuid)
- model_version: model & exact artifact id
- hw_target: e.g., a100-80gb, h100-112gb
- token_length_distribution: short/median/long buckets (counts)
- latency_ms: p50, p90, p99 as numbers
- throughput_rps: single-instance throughput numbers per batch size
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: normalized cost metric
- sample_prompt_hashes: up to 5 sample vectors (hashes)
- benchmark_commit: git sha for harness
- benchmark_trace_url: signed link to trace artifact

Dependencies: [list]
- ENG-23114 (benchmark harness contract changes)
- ENG-23899 (publish operator implementation)
- ENG-24202 (retention/cron job)
- PM-11258 (operational playbook observability-driven refresh)

Links and artifacts: [list]
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pm/perf-signature-operator
- Benchmark harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/1423
- Operator prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5789
- Verified registry (git): https://git.redwood.ai/verified-profiles/tree/mvp

Stakeholders and reviewers: [list]
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Priya Menon (Console PM)
- Eng: Miguel Ortega (owner), Liyun Zhao (Benchmark lead), Daniel Kim (Platform lead)
- SRE: Rowan Ellis
- Security/Legal: Hana Fitzgerald

Customer impact: medium
- This reduces false-positive regressions and shortens onboarding time for new models; initial rollout limited to internal model catalog to reduce risk.

Progress updates: [list]
- 2026-03-02: PM spec draft posted to Confluence; feedback requested from Benchmark and Platform.
- 2026-03-04: Benchmark team (Liyun) accepted telemetry contract; ENG-23114 created.
- 2026-03-07: Platform prototype operator created; initial validate/sign flow implemented (PR linked).
- 2026-03-09: Security review scheduled; signer key rotation notes added to spec.
- 2026-03-10: Cross-team sync; retention window adjusted from 9 to 12 months after cost analysis.

Risks and mitigations: [list]
- Risk: Indexing git-backed artifacts at scale could be slow. Mitigation: incremental indexer and batched reindex; migrate to DB only if not performant.
- Risk: Telemetry contract changes produce churn. Mitigation: schema versioning and backward-compatible fields; operator to accept v1/v2 during transition.
- Risk: Accidental archival of widely used profiles. Mitigation: add 'pinned' flag for high-usage models and require manual steward approval to archive.

Open questions: [list]
- Should enterprise customers see a customer-facing signature (signed with customer key) in MVP or wait for Private deployment support?
- Exact archival storage requirements for traces (S3 vs. internal artifact store).

Next steps: [list]
- Finish PM spec and circulate for final review (due 2026-03-12).
- Merge benchmark PR and platform operator prototype (target 2026-03-20).
- Create follow-up ticket to implement profile usage-based decay (PM- TBC).
acceptance_criteria: Operator validates complete signature payload including sample vectors
Published profiles include provenance (signer, commit, timestamp) and a link to benchmark run
Benchmark harness emits the telemetry contract and is merged
Retention encoded as scheduled job with alerts for staleness
Runbook reviewed by SRE, Security, and Legal
rollout_steps: MVP publish operator enabled for internal catalog only
Run 1-week shadow indexing to validate indexer performance
Enable auto-archive job in staging and validate unarchive flow
Enable console visibility (status + provenance) to internal testers
Gradual rollout to public catalog after 2 weeks of stability
